pages.head: Names in English
text: In English, a name has two parts. The first name comes first: Anna. The last name comes second: Smith. Together they make your full name: Anna Smith.

Many people have a nickname. A nickname is a short or friendly name. Robert is Bob. Elizabeth is Liz. William is Bill. Your friends call you by your nickname, but your teacher usually uses your first name.
When you meet someone, say: "Hello, I'm Anna. Nice to meet you." Then ask: "What's your name?"
tf: A full name has first name + last name.
Bob is a nickname for Robert.
Your teacher always uses your nickname.

pages.title: Names: fact file

facts.label: most common surname
facts.sub: in the UK and the USA

text: In English-speaking countries, people use first names very quickly. Teachers, bosses and neighbors often say 'Call me Tom.'
Titles like Mr., Ms. and Dr. are used with last names: Mr. Brown, Dr. Silva.
If you do not catch a name, it is polite to say: 'Sorry, what's your name again?'
